ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: At time 0, the velocity of the particle is 5 m/s
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure there are two coordinate graphs, A and B. In Figure A, the vertical axis is labeled v/(m·s^-1), and the horizontal axis is labeled t/s. The straight line rises from v=3 m/s at t=0 to v=6 m/s at t=2 s, and v=6 and t=2 are marked with dashed lines. In Figure B, the vertical axis is labeled s/m, and the horizontal axis is labeled t/s. The straight line descends from s=8 m at t=0 to s=0 m at t=2 s. Reasoning: Figure A represents the change of velocity in the x direction with time, so the velocity component in the x direction at time 0 is v_x0=3 m/s. Figure B represents the change of displacement in the y direction with time; the graph line is a straight line, so the velocity in the y direction equals the slope: v_y=(0-8)/(2-0)=-4 m/s. The x and y directions are perpendicular to each other, therefore the magnitude of the velocity at time 0 is v=sqrt(v_x0^2+v_y^2)=sqrt(3^2+(-4)^2)=5 m/s.
